ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two quadrilaterals in the figure. The vertices of the quadrilateral on the left are A, B, C, D, side AB is labeled x+1, and side CD is labeled x−1. The vertices of the quadrilateral on the right are E, F, G, H, side EF is labeled 8, and side GH is labeled 5. The angle markings show that A and E both have one arc, B corresponds to F, C corresponds to G, and D corresponds to H. Therefore the corresponding sides are AB ↔ EF, CD ↔ GH. Reasoning: The problem states that these two polygons are similar, so corresponding sides are proportional. From AB=x+1, EF=8, CD=x−1, GH=5, the proportion (x+1)/8 = (x−1)/5 can be set up. Cross multiplying gives 5(x+1)=8(x−1), that is, 5x+5=8x−8, so 13=3x, x=13/3. AB is required, therefore AB=x+1=13/3+1=16/3.
